\label{sec:abstract}
Near-minimal cosmological bounds on the summed neutrino mass $\sum m_\nu$ can shift under seemingly benign pipeline/likelihood updates, yet standard presentations rarely include lens-level stability diagnostics that distinguish cosmology from packaging effects. We address the inconsistency highlighted by \cite{arxiv2601_16277}, where swapping the SPT-3G 2018 TT/TE/EE likelihood for the later SPT-3G D1 release---analyzing essentially the same sky field---tightens $\sum m_\nu$ constraints and can move posteriors toward the physical boundary $\sum m_\nu=0$.

Our approach is to cast this lens swap as a packaging stability problem in the Six Birds / SBT formalism \cite{sixbirds_foundations,sixbirds_darkenergy}. We introduce a directional cross-lens audit functional, operationalize it via a profiled/localized/common-staging workflow, and demonstrate the resulting empirical stability picture under matched controls. Concretely, we (i) compute directional held-out mismatch statistics $\dchi_{B|A}$ and $\dchi_{A|B}$, (ii) localize mismatch by spectrum and multipole, (iii) repeat under a common-staging multipole-support control, and (iv) reproduce the $\sum m_\nu$ tightening under DESI DR2 BAO for two baselines (SPT-only+DESI; Planck-subset+PR4-lensing CMB baseline+DESI).

We find that cross-lens mismatch is large and asymmetric; profiling reduces but does not remove the failure; common-staging changes the profiled mismatch only at the few-percent level; and localization shows TT high-$\ell$ structure (roughly $\ell\sim2000$--$3000$) dominates within the overlap region. Under fixed BAO, swapping SPT2018$\rightarrow$D1 tightens the $\sum m_\nu$ 95\% upper bound by $\mathcal{O}(10^{-1},\mathrm{eV})$ in the SPT-only+DESI regime and by $\mathcal{O}(10^{-2},\mathrm{eV})$ in the Planck-subset baseline+DESI regime.

These artifacts turn an ambiguous parameter shift into a reproducible, localized diagnosis of lens disagreement and provide a disciplined contract for follow-up tests (including raw-data reprocessing diagnostics already emphasized by \cite{arxiv2601_16277}). We are explicit that identifying the pipeline root cause or establishing a definitive $\sum m_\nu$ value is not done here; our conclusions rely on audits of released likelihood objects under matched controls and the physical gate $\sum m_\nu\ge0$.

\label{sec:abstract}
Near-minimal cosmological bounds on the summed neutrino mass $\mnu$ can shift under seemingly benign pipeline/likelihood updates, yet standard presentations rarely include lens-level stability diagnostics that distinguish cosmology from packaging effects. We address the inconsistency highlighted by \cite{arxiv2601_16277}, where swapping the SPT-3G 2018 TT/TE/EE likelihood for the later SPT-3G D1 release---analyzing essentially the same sky field---tightens $\mnu$ constraints and can move posteriors toward the physical boundary $\mnu=0$.

Our approach is to cast this lens swap as a packaging stability problem in the Six Birds / SBT formalism \cite{sixbirds_foundations,sixbirds_darkenergy}. We introduce a directional cross-lens audit functional, operationalize it via a profiled/localized/common-staging workflow, and demonstrate the resulting empirical stability picture under matched controls. Concretely, we (i) compute directional held-out mismatch statistics $\dchi_{B|A}$ and $\dchi_{A|B}$, (ii) localize mismatch by spectrum and multipole, (iii) repeat under a common-staging multipole-support control, and (iv) reproduce the $\mnu$ tightening under DESI DR2 BAO for two baselines (SPT-only+DESI; Planck-subset+PR4-lensing CMB baseline+DESI).

We find that cross-lens mismatch is large and asymmetric; profiling reduces but does not remove the failure; common-staging changes the profiled mismatch only at the few-percent level; and localization shows TT high-$\ell$ structure (roughly $\ell\sim2000$--$3000$) dominates within the overlap region. Under fixed BAO, swapping SPT2018$\rightarrow$D1 tightens the $\mnu$ 95\% upper bound by $\mathcal{O}(10^{-1},\mathrm{eV})$ in the SPT-only+DESI regime and by $\mathcal{O}(10^{-2},\mathrm{eV})$ in the Planck-subset baseline+DESI regime.

These artifacts turn an ambiguous parameter shift into a reproducible, localized diagnosis of lens disagreement and provide a disciplined contract for follow-up tests (including raw-data reprocessing diagnostics already emphasized by \cite{arxiv2601_16277}). We are explicit that identifying the pipeline root cause or establishing a definitive $\mnu$ value is not done here; our conclusions rely on audits of released likelihood objects under matched controls and the physical gate $\mnu\ge0$.

Let parameters be partitioned as $\theta=(\phi,\eta_B)$ where $\phi$ denotes the shared parameters we hold fixed in the audit direction $B|A$ and $\eta_B$ denotes nuisance parameters specific to lens $B$. Define the profiled log-likelihood
\begin{equation}
  \log \widetilde{\mathcal{L}}_B(\phi) \;\equiv\; \max_{\eta_B}\, \log \mathcal{L}_B(\phi,\eta_B),
  \label{eq:profile_loglike}
\end{equation}
and the profiled directional mismatch
\begin{equation}
  \widetilde{\Delta \chi^2}_{B|A} \;\equiv\; -2\left[\log \widetilde{\mathcal{L}}_B(\hat\phi_A) - \log \widetilde{\mathcal{L}}_B(\hat\phi_B)\right],
  \label{eq:profile_dchi}
\end{equation}
where $\hat\phi_L$ is the shared-parameter component of the best-fit point under lens $L$.
In practice we approximate \cref{eq:profile_loglike} by profiling only a tractable subset of $B$'s nuisance parameters under a runtime cap; the intent is not to ``profile away'' all mismatch, but to reduce sensitivity to purely lens-specific packaging degrees of freedom.
In our implementation, the profiled set comprises the following calibration/beta parameters:
\begin{quote}\small\raggedright
\texttt{Tcal\_ext150},
\texttt{Tcal\_rel90},
\texttt{Tcal\_rel220},
\texttt{Ecal\_ext150},
\texttt{Ecal\_rel90},
\texttt{Ecal\_rel220},
\texttt{TT\_CIBClustering\_Alpha},
\texttt{TT\_CIB\_150x150},
\texttt{TT\_CIB\_150x220},
\texttt{TT\_CIB\_220x220},
\texttt{TT\_GalCirrus\_Alpha},
\texttt{TT\_GalCirrus\_Amp}.
\end{quote}
\noindent For the reverse direction, the capped set is:
\begin{quote}\small\raggedright
\texttt{TT\_tSZ\_CIB\_Corr\_Amp},
\texttt{TT\_tSZ\_CIB\_corr},
\texttt{Ecal150},
\texttt{Ecal220},
\texttt{Ecal90},
\texttt{TT\_CIBClustering\_Alpha},
\texttt{TT\_CIBClustering\_Amp},
\texttt{TT\_CIBClustering\_Beta},
\texttt{TT\_GalCirrus\_Alpha},
\texttt{TT\_GalCirrus\_Amp},
\texttt{TT\_GalCirrus\_Beta},
\texttt{TT\_Poisson\_150x150}
\end{quote}
\noindent (runtime-capped to 12 parameters; see run metadata).

conclusion: Consider a single nonnegative parameter m 0 (standing in for m_nu ) and suppose two independent packaged constraints yield approximately Gaussian log-likelihood contributions, L_i(m) = - (m-mu_i)^2 2sigma_i^2 + const, i∈\ 1,2\ , with sigma_i>0 . The combined (unconstrained) likelihood is proportional to a Gaussian with mean and variance mu_ = mu_1/sigma_1^2 + mu_2/sigma_2^2 1/sigma_1^2 + 1/sigma_2^2 , sigma_ ^2 = 1 1/sigma_1^2 + 1/sigma_2^2 . If the two packaged constraints are in tension, it is possible for mu_ < 0 even though the physical parameter space is m 0 . Enforcing the gate m 0 corresponds to truncating the Gaussian at 0, producing a (normalized) truncated density on [0,∈fty) . In that case the mode occurs at m_ mode = (0,mu_ ), so whenever the unconstrained optimum lies at mu_ 0 , the constrained mode is exactly at the boundary m=0 . This is the sense in which ``boundary modes'' (sometimes informally described as ``quasi-negative'' behavior) can arise: the negative optimum is not physical, but it is the optimizer's reconciliation point for incompatible packaged constraints, and truncation forces the packaged macro object to pile up at the boundary. \subsection{Interpretation for $\sum m_\nu$ under lens swaps}
This toy model does not claim that any specific real-data run must exhibit a boundary mode, and indeed our baseline+DESI production runs have near-zero boundary fraction for $\sum m_\nu$ (\cref{sec:results-mnu}). Rather, it clarifies why boundary motion can be a \emph{generic symptom} of packaging instability when a hard physical gate is present. In the SBT framing, the boundary is a gating constraint (P2), and strong boundary sensitivity is naturally interpreted as an indicator that the completion is being asked to reconcile incompatible packaged summaries (a route mismatch symptom, P3), especially when the mismatch is localized in the overlap region (\cref{sec:results-audits}).

This note is deliberately scoped and has several limitations:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, itemsep=2pt]
  \item \textbf{Completion/nuisance choices.} Our production $\sum m_\nu$ chains use a minimal nuisance sampling set for computational tractability, and our profiled audits optimize only a runtime-capped subset of nuisance parameters (\cref{sec:profiled-audit}). Broader nuisance freedom and alternative priors can shift tight sub-0.1\,eV bounds.
  \item \textbf{Likelihood and baseline implementation details.} While we match the Planck-subset+PR4-lensing structure described in \cite{arxiv2601_16277}, small implementation choices (e.g.\ the low-$\ell$ EE variant available in a given likelihood wrapper) can propagate into tight derived bounds.
  \item \textbf{Finite compute and crude diagnostics.} Some of our MCMC diagnostics for $\sum m_\nu$ (ESS and split-$\hat R$ proxies \cite{gelman_rubin1992,vehtari2021_rhat}) are necessarily crude given the expense of CMB+Boltzmann runs. Our aim is to reproduce qualitative behavior and provide audit localization, not to provide definitive converged limits beyond what is needed for the lens-swap comparison.
  \item \textbf{Audits over likelihood objects, not raw maps.} Our analyses operate on released likelihood objects. As such, the audits identify where the packaged summaries disagree, but they do not by themselves pinpoint whether the origin is calibration, beam/transfer functions, foreground modeling, mapmaking, or other pipeline components.
\end{itemize}
